Name: WordPress
Description: WAF in detection mode, uptime monitor on the home page, nosniff header
Note: A starting point, review it before use. Large uploads and plugins can trigger WAF detections; they are only logged until you switch to Block. In WordPress set both addresses to https://your-domain.

Name: Nextcloud
Description: WebSocket on, WAF in detection mode, uptime monitor on /status.php
Note: A starting point, review it before use. WebDAV and large uploads pass through unchanged. In Nextcloud add this proxy to trusted_proxies and the domain to trusted_domains in config.php, and set overwriteprotocol to https.

Name: Home Assistant
Description: WebSocket on (required for the live UI), WAF in detection mode, uptime monitor
Note: A starting point, review it before use. Home Assistant refuses proxied requests until http: in configuration.yaml has use_x_forwarded_for: true and this proxy listed under trusted_proxies.

Name: Jellyfin
Description: WebSocket on, uptime monitor on /health, no WAF or rate limit changes
Note: A starting point, review it before use. Streaming makes many range requests, so no rate limit is set. Add this proxy under Known proxies in the Jellyfin network settings so client addresses are correct.

Name: Plex
Description: WebSocket on, uptime monitor on /identity, no WAF or rate limit changes
Note: A starting point, review it before use. Streaming makes many range requests, so no rate limit is set. In Plex add the public address under Network, Custom server access URLs.

Name: Grafana
Description: WebSocket on (Grafana Live), WAF in detection mode, uptime monitor on /api/health
Note: A starting point, review it before use. In grafana.ini set root_url to the public https address. Grafana Live checks the Origin header, so add the address to live.allowed_origins if live panels fail.

Name: Vaultwarden
Description: WebSocket on (sync notifications), WAF in detection mode, uptime monitor on /alive
Note: A starting point, review it before use. Set DOMAIN to the public https address in Vaultwarden. Restrict /admin with an access rule or a path rule if you enable the admin page.

Name: Gitea or GitLab
Description: WebSocket on, WAF in detection mode, uptime monitor on the home page
Note: A starting point, review it before use. Git pushes over HTTPS send large bodies, which the WAF does not inspect past its limit. Set ROOT_URL (Gitea) or external_url (GitLab) to the public https address.

Name: Portainer
Description: WebSocket on (container console), WAF in detection mode, uptime monitor on /api/system/status
Note: A starting point, review it before use. Portainer controls your containers: also pick an access rule and an authentication provider. If it only serves HTTPS with its own certificate, turn on TLS for the upstream in the upstream settings.

Name: JSON API
Description: Rate limit 100 req/s per IP (burst 200), request id header, WAF in detection mode, WebSocket off
Note: A starting point, review it before use. Tune the rate limit to the real traffic of your clients. Set the health check path to an endpoint of your API.

Name: Static website
Description: Browser hardening headers, exploit blocking, light rate limit, WebSocket off
Note: A starting point, review it before use. Fits a site that only serves files. If the site uses WebSockets or is embedded in frames of other sites, adjust the result.

Name: Strict admin panel
Description: Rate limit 10 req/s per IP (burst 20), WAF in block mode, exploit blocking, browser hardening headers
Note: A starting point, review it before use. This preset does not turn on authentication by itself: choose an authentication provider and an access rule for the rule. The WAF can block legitimate admin actions, so watch the WAF log.
